Dûr-Vazhatun (暗望所, I03)

Verification: 2026-10-13 · local Mod v1.37.5.0 · English scoring-table region: Serpentspine.

Narrative quality: High; primarily based on local narrative text; mission-tree length: 36 directly defined missions; mission update context: current installed v1.37.5.0; the actual author's last update time was not verified; uniqueness: High; observation knowledge, observation efficiency, and Hold excavation form an independent research loop; time spent waiting (lower is smoother): Medium; diplomacy, research, or event-state gates apply; early pressure: 68/100, not an in-game-tested difficulty; expansion demand: 66/100, driven by both warfare and management.

v2.1: E57 · A58 · M/T82 · I94 · P38; values: Neutral (56), trajectory: mixed. The five axes are not a four-letter type; see the separate v2.2 conditional profile for the route.

Player overview

Dûr-Vazhatun is a dwarven Hold that treats stargazing as a national vocation. You first rebuild the scholarly centre, repair the roads, and organise expeditions, then accumulate astral knowledge through continuing observations. The problem is that knowledge does not guarantee safety: the ancient Hold's downfall and the present investigation gradually become one horror story. It is best suited to players who like research, ruins, and mystery; if you want a dwarven industrial pipeline that simply unlocks positive rewards, this place will make you uneasy.

Historical background and formation route

【Established history in the Wiki supplement】 The English offline page calls Dûr-Vazhatun the Home of the Dark Sky Watchers, emphasising the ancient observatory and astronomical tradition, and connects the ancient downfall to Astral Terror. The page's 6284 BA date and the refugees' destination are supplements from this particular revision's worldbuilding; they are not a date guarantee for the current mission future and not an opening statement that the player already knows the truth.

【Local identity】 I03's country-history file lists Sapphire Dwarf culture, Ancestor Worship, a republic template, and capital 4020, but this is a country template and does not prove that I03 already exists on the 1444 map. The actual entry is the formation decision: a qualifying dwarven adventurer must own 4020, have the relevant reform and administrative conditions, satisfy the core, peace, administrative technology 7, at least three cities, and other formation checks, with a separate time exception retained by the script.

On formation, the country changes to I03, Sapphire culture, and that capital, and swaps in a non-generic mission tree. No unique dedicated predecessor has been verified, so the encyclopedia does not draw an imaginary 1444 territory for it or force any adventurer's name to be treated as Dûr-Vazhatun.

Distinctive mechanics and campaign rhythm

The basic layer is still the dwarven Hold: excavation, construction, restoring connections, and securing room to operate in the mountains. The unique missions do not reduce development to income alone; excavation and expansion are also tied to astral knowledge. The observation system tracks knowledge, observation efficiency, and completed observations; yearly observations build the stock, while later missions check and spend knowledge. The object of management therefore includes the city, research, and long-term risk at the same time.

Scholarly revival, contact with the outside world, the eastern frontier, and dedicated expeditions change the rhythm. Expeditions involving damestear and ancient ruins keep the source of knowledge from being just a variable that grows while waiting. You still need an army and a treasury, but the clearest feedback is not conquering a plain; it is making the entire country run around observing, interpreting, and pursuing the past.

This is also why it is not simply a “magic superpower”. Magical orientation and theme intensity are separate scores: the country clearly leans toward esoteric research, and that research is extremely important; but each astronomical activity cannot be treated as a freely cast spell, nor can the magic direction be given a perfect score merely because of the theme.

The mission tree's future

【Mission future】 The current 36 directly defined missions connect scholarly reconstruction, astral information, knowledge spending, expeditions, and investigation of the ancient downfall. The closer the player gets to the old secrets, the more Astral Terror must be managed: the disaster and its related events turn fear, social unrest, and violence into continuing pressure. Strange creatures and madness in the player-facing story should be tied to these scripted entry points, not used to claim that every save necessarily experiences the same intensity.

The story includes extreme calls to destroy the Hold, but that does not establish a fixed, freely selectable ending in which the country is destroyed. This batch did not exhaust every disaster option, so it does not manufacture two mutually exclusive personalities, “rational scholars” and “destroyer mad king”. The ancient tragedy, the contemporary investigation, and the later disaster must also remain separate: the encyclopedia describes what the player may uncover, rather than rewriting the future as 1444 history.

National personality and values

Its central personality combines building with exploration, relatively concentrated institutions, and mysterious research at the centre of society. Compared with the Glass Lords' technological-industrial direction, Dûr-Vazhatun leans more toward cosmic mysteries; compared with the explicit domination of an isolated personality, the evidence here supports dangerous exploration and loss of control, not an unverified intention to dominate.

Its values are provisionally Neutral, not because “cosmic horror is evil”, but because public scholarship and urban management serve public ends while the disaster damages social safety, and the responsibility boundary of some actions still needs clarification. No sufficiently clear independent phase with a difference of 20 points or more was confirmed, so no phase scores are invented from the atmosphere of horror. Players looking for a warm, stable scientific utopia should understand that this country's theme is not safe progress.

Community experience, recommendation, and cautions

【Community views】 A 2023 plot-question thread and a 2026 dwarven-narrative discussion both put its sense of wonder and storytelling near the centre. Player opinion can help decide whether the horror theme suits someone, but cannot replace current disaster conditions or mission rewards. This batch did not obtain a substantive independent official development diary about this country; an author being mentioned in other diaries does not count as an official introduction to Dûr-Vazhatun.

It is recommended for players who like Hold management, dedicated research resources, ruin expeditions, and gradually unfolding mysteries. The cautions are disaster management, long-horizon resource planning, and dark narrative; no in-game balance testing was performed in this batch. The English Wiki can supplement the ancient background, but the complete event endings and all disaster conditions remain incomplete; search snippets are not used to turn those gaps into certainty.

Sources, retrieval scope, and unresolved items are listed on the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and scripted effects. Traditions apply when this idea group is adopted, the seven ideas unlock in order as the group is invested in, and the ambition applies after all seven ideas are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, governmental, and mission rewards are not mixed into the values. A new idea set after formation is not automatically added on top of the old one. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the content has already happened in 1444.

Dûr-Vazhatun (I03) — Sapphire Ideas

Tradition: Sapphire Traditions

Effect: Innovativeness gain: +0.5; Army maintenance modifier: -10%.

Idea 1: Scholars of the Dwarovar

Dûr-Vazhatun was once the hub for the brightest and most eccentric minds in Aul-Dwarov to gather, argue, and search for truth together. Though many of their names and works have been lost to time, the empty libraries and broken laboratories they left behind bear witness that genius existed here once, and inspires us that it could exist again.

Effect: Research cost: -5%.

Idea 2: Skygazers

'What is the sky but a great cavern filled with sparkling diamonds?', a common saying amongst the Sapphire Dwarves

Dwarves generally hate the sky. The sky knows no bounds. It goes on forever. Solid ground however has a beginning and end. It's reliable. It's safe.

The sapphire dwarves think differently, for surely there must be an end to the great dark beyond? And if dwarves have a love of gems then surely they must desire the shiniest objects of all: stars.

Effect: Idea cost: -10%.

Idea 3: The Setzunkhûpa

"Dûr-Vazhatun" means "Home of the Dark Sky Watchers", or "The Observatory" in simple Common. Atop the highest peak of the northern Serpentspine lies possibly the greatest achievement of Aul-Dwarov; the giant stone and iron sphere known as the "Setzunkhûpa", or the "Sky Dome". On clear nights when the stars are shimmering the sphere will open, quaking the very mountainside itself, clearing the way for the massive telescope inside.

Crafted by Mellegar the Inventor from the rune-strengthened glass of Orlghelovar, this observatory can observe the celestial wonders of the world in ways the rest of Halann can barely dream of. Unfortunately, the wonders of the Setsunkhûpa led to nightmares that brought low Dûr-Vazhatun in the past. Increasing use of the observatory led to a malady called "Astral Terror" which inevitably led into madness and hysteria about 'what lies behind the stars'.

Effect: Free diplomatic policy: +1.

Idea 4: Research-led Surface Colonies

Even dwarves are children of the stars, many of them spent their entire lives underground, but the Sapphire Dwarves funded many surface colonies. Research demanded them to push to bounds never before broken, and settle the surface so that their children may sleep gazing at the night sky.

Effect: Number of colonists: +1.

Idea 5: The Ruminators

The Ruminators are a series of ruined sculptures through the Hold of the greatest scholars of old Dûr-Vazhatun locked in deep thought, pondering the greatest of puzzles of their age. From still-famous names like Mellegar the Inventor and Beddugr Melmarn to dwarves whose names and accomplishments have been lost to time. We should repair these great works and honour the greatest of our own scholars with new ones. The Ruminators can once again serve as a reminder of all the discoveries and philosophies created in these halls and the everlasting fame awarded to our brightest minds.

Effect: Global institution spread: +10%; Institution embracement cost: -10%.

Idea 6: Students of Mind and Sky

Since the beginning of our history we have been fascinated by the sky and stars, dreaming to uncover their secrets. The grand archives were filled to the brim with research papers, research teams were sent out to the surface, laboratories were dedicated to astronomy, and the great observatory was constantly used to study the sky. From all over Aul-Dwarov we were famous for our scholars and astronomers, ever looked upon with jealousy among their peers thanks to the breakthroughs they made revolutionising their fields.

Effect: Advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 7: Sapphire Wit

We are a home to many impassioned scholars, and thus also to many an impassioned scholarly debate. As proper decorum befitting a distinguished scholar of Dûr-Vazhatun must be observed at all times, it has become increasingly common for these debaters to express their true feelings toward one another through more subtle words. Many of our greatest thinkers pride themselves on how deep and sharp their words can cut their opponents, all without ever saying anything impolite or disrespectful of course.

Effect: Power projection from insults: +1.

Ambition: Sapphire Ambition

Effect: Army attrition: -20%.
